definitions.geographic_resource_breadth: count of native extant non-doubtful WCVP-v13 WGSRPD3 units in the union of resolved larval hosts
definitions.rank_discordance: percentile rank of geographic resource breadth minus percentile rank of host-family breadth
definitions.specialist_wide: host-family count == 1 and geographic resource breadth >= panel 75th percentile
definitions.generalist_narrow: host-family count >= 6 and geographic resource breadth <= panel 25th percentile

host_taxonomy_lower_bound_adequate_subse.definition: resolved HOSTS-WCVP host-species count >= LepTraits NumberOfHostplantFamilies

ecological_interpretation.asymmetry: Taxonomic specialists can have very broad geographic resource opportunity. Apparent generalist-but-geographically-narrow cases disappear under the conservative host-taxonomy completeness floor.
ecological_interpretation.mechanistic_reading: Using few host families does not imply a geographically restricted larval resource base: a specialist may use many host species within one family and/or hosts with broad native distributions.
ecological_interpretation.consequence: Butterfly specialization should be treated as at least two axes: taxonomic diet breadth and geographic resource breadth.
